title: Unemployment Benefit Claims — Computation of a Dependency Disallowance Reduction
content:
The reduction booked by a dependency disallowance on an Unemployment Benefit Claims record is computed as follows.

1. **Redetermined allowance.** The program's dependency allowance per dependent times the dependents now on record, counting no more than the program's maximum number of dependents, rounded to the cent.
2. **Allowance decrease.** The dependency allowance on the claim less the redetermined allowance, never below zero.
3. **Reduction.** The allowance decrease times the program's maximum duration weeks, rounded down to the whole dollar and never below zero.

The decrease is found first and then multiplied by the weeks; the rounding down to the whole dollar is applied to the product.

## Records read

The dependents now on record and the dependency allowance on the claim are read from the claim; the per-dependent amount, the maximum number of dependents and the maximum duration weeks are the program's scheduled figures.

## Worked example (hypothetical claim, Regular State Unemployment Insurance figures)

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Allowance on the claim (set for 3 dependents) | 45.00 |
| Dependents now on record | 2 |
| Redetermined allowance: 15.00 times 2 | 30.00 |
| Allowance decrease: 45.00 less 30.00 | 15.00 |
| Reduction: 15.00 times 26 weeks | 390.00 |

An allowance on the claim already at or below the redetermined allowance gives a reduction of zero.
